messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Canary health degraded for deployment redwood-inference-api (canary 2026-04-12-0.3.7) — websocket error rate > 10% across live sessions. Pager routed to Raj (oncall).

Raj (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing 502/503s from model-serve websocket connections, sessions not dropping on pod termination.

Maria Chen: Confirmed spike in us-west around 14:02 UTC. Canary weight ~25%. Error rate concentrated on /v1/stream/ws.

Sasha Ivanov: Auto-rollback kicked off but it's stuck in `drain-wait` state for ~10m. Logs show many long-lived connection_ids refusing to close. Example: `connection_id=abc123 session_age=00:42:13`

Raj (oncall): Can we flip feature flag `use-new-ws-handoff` to stop new connections from being routed to the canary while we drain? @Oliver Grant

Oliver Grant: On it. Running: ```ffctl toggle use-new-ws-handoff --env=prod --off --actor=oliver.grant```
Oliver Grant: :white_check_mark: FF toggled off. Routing control acknowledged by router; new ws connections should go to stable.

support-bot: Customer-impact: 3 customers reported intermittent session glitches, no broad outage. Support queue: #cust-335. Escalated to SEs.

Maria Chen: Auto-rollback still shows `drain-wait`. If sessions don't drain we should do manual rollback to stable to stop new traffic and free resources. Proposed command: ```redwood deploy rollback --deployment=redwood-api --target=stable --reason="canary ws leak"```

Raj (oncall): Quick attempt: try forcing connection close on the canary pods before rollback: ```kubectl exec -n prod canary-pod-7f4 -- /app/drain-connections --timeout=30s```

Sasha Ivanov: Ran drain on one pod; connections persist. Looks like client SDK v1.2.9 has an aggressive reconnect logic that keeps reattaching. That's preventing graceful drain.

Oliver Grant: Understood. Proceeding with manual rollback now to stop traffic to canary and reduce surface area. Executing: ```redwood deploy rollback --deployment=redwood-api --tag=stable-20260412 --force --actor=oliver.grant```

incident-bot: Rollback job queued: job_id=rb-1741239999-1. Status: running.

Raj (oncall): I'll hand verification to Maria once rollback completes. Maria, can you run the smoke+canary checks?

Maria Chen: Copy. Running smoke: ```/usr/local/bin/smoke --suite=canary-check --endpoint=https://api.redwood.ai/health --expect=200 --retries=3```

Sasha Ivanov: Routing metrics shifting: canary weight -> 0 over ~2 minutes. Websocket session count for canary pods dropping from 120 -> 6 currently. Looks like clients finally gave up reconnecting to the canary.

support-bot: Customer-impact update: affected sessions reduced, no new tickets in last 10m. Notified impacted customers with ETA.

incident-bot: Rollback job finished: job_id=rb-1741239999-1. Status: success. Completed at ts=1741240200.

Maria Chen: Verification: health checks green, 200s stable, p50/p95 latency back to baseline. Ran regression evals: ```evals run prompt-suite/canary-smoke --subset=quick``` -> pass.

Raj (oncall): Postmortem tasks: 1) Patch SDK reconnect behavior to respect drain signals (owner: Oliver) 2) Add a hard drain timeout to auto-rollback to avoid permanent `drain-wait` (owner: Sasha) 3) Add telemetry alert when websocket drain duration > 5m (owner: Sasha) 4) Improve customer comms template for long-lived sessions (owner: Support).

Sasha Ivanov: I'll open INFRA-679 for drain timeout & telemetry, include proposed rollout plan.

Oliver Grant: I'll coordinate SDK patch with eng-ml and cut a 1.2.10 patch.

support-bot: Noted owners and tasks. Routing to triage board.

Raj (oncall): Closing active paging thread. We'll run a short blameless postmortem tomorrow. Thanks all for fast responses. :thumbsup:
